lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Marcio Ferreira Santos | Lesson 2 -- Your Results in English

listenings.text: Good afternoon, and thank you for joining the second session of the forum. It is a pleasure to introduce our next speaker. Laura Bennett has worked in pricing for eighteen years, and she has led the pricing team at Northfield Grocers since two thousand and sixteen. In two thousand and eighteen she launched the first category pricing model in the company, and revenue grew by six percent in one year. She has spoken at this forum three times, and every time the room has been full. Today she will talk about what happens when a pricing model meets a real store. Please welcome Laura Bennett.

Hi Marcio, it is Paul. You asked me how to answer the question about your best professional result, so here is the short version. Interviewers do not want a list. They want a story with three parts. First, the context: where you were and what the problem was. Second, the action: what you did, in the past simple, because that part is finished. Third, the result: what changed, and this is where the present perfect helps, because the result is still true today. Keep the whole story under ninety seconds. And please, give one number. One number is worth more than five adjectives. Talk soon.

extra_audio.text: Laura Bennett started her career as a store manager in Ohio. She joined Northfield Grocers in two thousand and sixteen. In two thousand and eighteen, she led the first category pricing rollout in the company. Revenue grew by six percent in twelve months. Two years later, her team delivered a cost reduction of eleven percent.

paras: Laura Bennett is the Vice President of Pricing at Northfield Grocers, a food retail group with four hundred stores in the United States. She has worked in pricing for eighteen years, and she has been at Northfield since 2016.

Her track record is unusual. In 2018, she led the first rollout of a category pricing model in the company, and the impact was immediate: revenue grew by six percent in twelve months. Two years later, her team delivered a cost reduction of eleven percent, and they did it without closing a single store.

Laura has published two papers on price elasticity, and she has spoken at this forum three times. She often says that the hardest part of her job is not the model, but the conversation: the numbers do not defend themselves. She did not study economics. She started her career as a store manager in Ohio, and she still visits ten stores every quarter.
